Guideline: Use Modern CSS linear() Function for True Spring Overshoot
Description: CSS cubic-bezier() can only have one inflection excursion. CSS linear() allows multi-point spring approximations natively on the compositor thread.
Do: Define reusable --spring-bounce and --spring-snappy custom properties using linear()
Don't: Load a 40KB JS physics library just for a badge pop or modal entrance
Code Bad: transition: transform 300ms linear; /* Robotic constant speed */

Guideline: Use Web Animations API (element.animate) for One-Shot Bursts
Description: WAAPI animations run on the compositor, don't require toggling CSS classes on/off with setTimeout, and resolve with a clean .finished Promise.
Do: Use el.animate(keyframes, options) for ripples, error shakes, hitstop releases, and neighbor nudges
Don't: Add and remove temporary animation classes with fragile setTimeout durations
Code Good: await el.animate([{ transform: 'scale(0.94)' }, { transform: 'scale(1.04)' }, { transform: 'scale(1)' }], { duration: 260, easing: 'cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)' }).finished;

Description: Smoothly animate unknown-height panels without max-height timing bugs.
Do: Transition grid-template-rows: 0fr -> 1fr with an inner overflow-hidden wrapper
Don't: Transition max-height: 0 -> 2000px (causes huge delay when collapsing short content)
Code Good: .panel { display: grid; grid-template-rows: 0fr; transition: grid-template-rows 240ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .panel.open { grid-template-rows: 1fr; }
